weakness.emptyAnalysis: Weakness analysis activates once you submit 5 or more pieces of writing.
weakness.insightHeadline: You can look at the {label} area first.
weakness.insightDisclaimer: This is an estimate based on trends in your recent answers. Your actual weaknesses may shift with future practice.
weakness.insightWhyTitle: Why look at this area first?

grammar.why: When sentence rules waver, even good ideas can come across less precisely.
grammar.example: Tenses, particles, and connectors often get mixed up within an answer.
grammar.strategy: Rewrite in short sentences and try the same expression in a different tense.

vocab.why: A narrow word choice leads to repeating the same meaning, weakening your answer's persuasiveness.
vocab.example: You may repeat only easy words or pick expressions that fit the context less well.
vocab.strategy: While solving recommended problems, note two synonymous expressions each time.

structure.why: When structure falls apart, the link between claim and evidence becomes less clear to the reader.
structure.example: The order of intro, evidence, and conclusion may get swapped, or one paragraph may mix several ideas.
structure.strategy: Before writing, jot down one main claim and two supporting points.

content.why: Thin content leaves your claims unsupported, making it hard to earn points.
content.example: You may repeat the same point without examples or evidence.
content.strategy: In recommended problems, practice adding one example to each claim.

expression.why: Monotonous expression makes it hard to convey the same meaning in varied ways.
expression.example: You may repeat similar expressions or have awkward transitions.
expression.strategy: While solving recommended problems, write two alternative expressions each time.

topic_fit.why: Drifting off topic makes it hard to score, even if the sentences are correct.
topic_fit.example: Background explanation may run longer than what the prompt asked for.
topic_fit.strategy: Reread the prompt, check the required conditions, then trim your answer.

fallback.why: This area scored low in your recent answers, so checking it first can help.
fallback.example: It's worth checking whether the same kind of mistake keeps recurring.
fallback.strategy: Solve recommended problems and revise your answer once more.

help.empty: There are no writing tips for this type yet.
help.tips51_0Body: Write a single sentence that flows naturally with the surrounding ones.
help.tips51_1Body: If the prompt is formal, match it with the formal -습니다/-ㅂ니다 endings.
help.tips51_2Body: Write only the essentials concisely, without unnecessary modifiers.
help.tips52_0Body: Align your connecting expressions so the two blanks form one flow.
help.tips52_1Body: Check that subject, predicate, and tense all agree.
help.tips52_2Body: Make clear what demonstratives like this/that/those refer to.
help.tips53_0Body: Cite the numerical changes in the graph/table directly as evidence.
help.tips53_1Body: Write in a three-part structure: intro, body, conclusion.
help.tips53_2Body: Wrap up with just the essentials within 200-300 characters.
help.tips54_0Body: State your stance clearly in the introduction.
help.tips54_1Body: Support the body with two or more distinct pieces of evidence.
help.tips54_2Body: Link paragraphs smoothly with however, therefore, and also.
